notes:
CIRCUIT: parallel RLC driven by a 4 mA DC current source. One rectangular loop: top rail y~372 from x~182 to x~632, bottom rail y~595 from x~185 to x~635, with four vertical branches - I-DC (x~183), R 2ohm (x~332), C 5mF (x~488), L 1mH (x~634) - and a GND symbol hanging below the bottom rail at x~492. Only two nodes exist.

NET MAP:
  n1 = the top rail. Terminals: R#0.t0 (top lead, x=332 y=446), C#1.t1 (top lead, x=489 y=456), I-DC#2.t0 (top lead, x=181 y=458 -> up and right along y~374), L#3.t0 (top lead, x=632 y=468).
  0  = the bottom rail plus the stub down to the GND symbol. Terminals: R#0.t1 (bottom lead, x~336 y=545 down to the rail at (338,598)), C#1.t0 (bottom lead x=488 y=499 down to (490,591)), I-DC#2.t1 (x=184 y=512), L#3.t1 (x=635 y=554), GND#4.t0 (x=492 y=611).

JUDGEMENT CALLS / SITE DECISIONS:
  S14 (491,594) deg=4 CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. The capacitor's lower lead runs straight down through the bottom rail and on to the GND symbol. inkmap at (491,594) shows a plain crossing: strokes stay ~3 px wide through the intersection, no blob, no hop or jog. Junction by the ink prior, and forced by electrics: read as a crossing, the capacitor's bottom lead + GND would form an island with no return path to the source and the whole bottom rail (I-DC, R, L) would float with no ground reference. Junction it is; this is also the only place the drawing grounds itself.
  S0 (482,373) deg=3 CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the capacitor's upper lead ends on the top rail. A T is a junction by definition. Read as anything else the capacitor's top lead would be a one-terminal net.
  S15 (338,598) deg=3 -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the resistor's lower lead ends on the bottom rail.
  S2 (533,492), S4 (564,494), S7 (360,507) -> not electrical. These are strokes of the handwritten value labels '5mF' and '2ohm' brushing the component boxes; left at the default, and after the port fixes below no terminal lands on them, so they carry no terminal.

PORT / TERMINAL FIXES:
  C#1: the tracer had t1 on port p2 @ (523,501), which is ink of the handwritten '5mF' label, giving a one-terminal net n3. Repointed t1 to p1 @ (489,456), the real upper lead (visible in the comps crop leaving the top of the plate). t0 stays on p0 @ (488,499), the real lower lead.
  R#0: the tracer had t1 on port p2 @ (352,511), a stroke of the handwritten '2ohm' label, giving a one-terminal net n2. The resistor's real lower lead exists in the wire graph (edge e24, (335,551)->(338,595), joining the bottom rail at S15) but the annotated box swallowed the stub so no port candidate was generated for it. t1 therefore set to null and pinned with manual_nets 0.1 = '0'; verified in the pixels that the lead below the resistor box runs unbroken from y=545 to the bottom rail at y=598.

BROKEN-INK MERGE:
  merge ['2.0','0.0'] - the top rail is drawn as one line but the scan has a ~15 px faded gap at y~374 between x=314 (end of the run from the current source, edge e2) and x=330 (corner of the run to the resistor, edge e1). Verified with inkmap/zoom at (321,374): both segments are collinear at the same y and the left one is uniformly faint, i.e. light pen pressure lost by thresholding, not a deliberate open. Without the merge the I-DC top terminal is a one-terminal net (n4) and the current source drives an open circuit, which is electrically impossible.

RESULT: 5 components, 2 nets, ERC clean. No class looks wrong: the up-arrow-in-a-circle labelled 4mA is an I-DC, the zigzag a resistor, the two parallel plates a capacitor, the coil an inductor.
